title: Lag Monitor
description: Main-thread lag of browser pages, from the lag library: native-histogram metrics in Mimir, events in Loki and the traces of the page views in Tempo.

list.name: service_name
list.label: Service
list.description: The service.name resource attribute. Mimir promotes it to the service_name label. Loki indexes it.

list.name: instance
list.label: Page load
list.description: One page load: one SDK instance (service.instance.id, the instance label of Mimir). With one page load, each panel and each annotation shows only that page. The Page loads table sets it.

list.name: session_id
list.label: Session
list.description: The start of a session.id. The Page loads table shows the page loads of the matching sessions.

list.name: navigation_type
list.label: Navigation type
list.description: How the page view started. Used by the Web Vitals panels.

panels.title: Active page loads
panels.description: Page loads (SDK instances) that sent drift samples in the minute before each point. Each page load has its own service.instance.id.

panels.title: Drift p95
panels.description: The 95th percentile of the drift lag of all page loads.

panels.title: Heartbeat delay p95
panels.description: The 95th percentile of the worker heartbeat delivery delay: the lag that a random event sees.

panels.title: INP p75
panels.description: Interaction to Next Paint, 75th percentile of the page views in the time range. Good: 200 ms or less. Poor: more than 500 ms.

panels.title: Hangs
panels.description: Main-thread hangs that the workers detected in the time range.

panels.title: Stalls
panels.description: Very long samples (hangs and suspends) in the time range.

panels.title: Drift lag p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The lag of each window of chained timeouts (about 100 ms): its duration minus the idle duration of its steps. Each main-thread block in the window adds to it.

panels.title: Drift baseline: timer granularity
panels.description: The idle duration of one timer step: the mean of the recent steps that are not blocks. An increase needs a probe that shows an idle thread, thus a sustained load does not change it. It is the timer granularity of the browser and the operating system. DriftLag subtracts it.

panels.title: Drift windows per second
panels.description: Windows that DriftLag recorded each second, for all page loads. Windows of hidden or frozen pages are discarded.

panels.title: Macrotask queue delay p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The time that a zero-delay timeout waits in the task queue. Each page load measures one sample every 5 seconds.

panels.title: Scheduling latency p50, by primitive
panels.description: The median latency of each scheduling primitive. The microtask latency stays near 0 and is the baseline.

panels.title: Scheduling latency p99, by primitive
panels.description: The 99th percentile latency of each scheduling primitive. A high macrotask or MessageChannel value shows a busy task queue.

panels.title: Heartbeat delivery delay: the lag that a random event sees
panels.description: The primary lag estimator. A worker sends a heartbeat each second from its own thread. The delay is the time that the heartbeat waited for the main thread. Heartbeats arrive at random times, as user events do.

panels.title: Worker self-lag
panels.description: The lateness of the worker's own heartbeat timer. A high value shows that the worker itself did not run, so its heartbeat delays are not reliable then.

panels.title: Worker clock offset
panels.description: The absolute offset between the worker clock and the main-thread clock, from the clock synchronization exchange.

panels.title: Hangs per minute, by outcome
panels.description: Main-thread hangs that the workers detected: the main thread did not acknowledge heartbeats. Abandoned: the page closed or crashed during the hang. The next page of the origin, another open page of the origin, or the page itself at its close reported it (lag.hang.source).

panels.title: Hang duration p50 / p95, by outcome
panels.description: The duration of each hang. For an abandoned hang, the duration until the worker saw the hang for the last time, or until the end of the page.

panels.title: Stalls per minute, by kind
panels.description: Very long samples. A hang has no evidence of a suspend. A suspend overlaps evidence that the system stopped (for example, the device slept).

panels.title: Stall duration p50 / p95, by kind
panels.description: The duration of each very long sample.

panels.title: Samples discarded per minute, by reason
panels.description: Samples that a monitor did not record, because the page was hidden or frozen, or the system was suspended during the measurement window.

panels.title: Clock jumps per minute, by kind and direction
panels.description: Discontinuities between the wall clock and the monotonic clock. Suspend: the monotonic clock stopped while the device slept. Step: the system clock changed.

panels.title: Clock skew p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The absolute difference between Date.now() and the absolute monotonic clock (timeOrigin plus performance.now()).

panels.title: performance.now() resolution
panels.description: The resolution of performance.now() of the page loads in the time range. Each page load measures it one time. Cross-origin isolated pages get 5 µs.

panels.title: LoAF blocking duration p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The blocking duration of each long animation frame: the time over 50 ms of its long tasks.

panels.title: LoAF duration p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The total duration of each long animation frame.

panels.title: Long animation frames per minute
panels.description: Long animation frames of all page loads, each minute.

panels.title: LoAF attribution: blocking time by script (events)
panels.description: From the lag.long_animation_frame events (frames that block 150 ms or more). The script is the script that blocked the frame most.

targets.expr: sum by (script_invoker_type, script_invoker, script_source_url) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", event_name="lag.long_animation_frame"} | service_instance_id=~"$instance" | keep script_invoker_type, script_invoker, script_source_url, blocking_duration_ms | unwrap blocking_duration_ms [$__range]))

sum by (script_invoker_type, script_invoker, script_source_url) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", event_name="lag.long_animation_frame"} | service_instance_id=~"$instance" | keep script_invoker_type, script_invoker, script_source_url [$__range]))

panels.title: Event duration p95, by interaction type
panels.description: The duration of each interaction event of 16 ms or more, from the input to the next paint.

panels.title: Event phases p95
panels.description: Where the time of an interaction goes: the input delay before the handlers, the processing time of the handlers, and the presentation delay to the next paint.

panels.title: Interactions per minute, by interaction type
panels.description: Interaction events of 16 ms or more, each minute.

panels.title: Layout shift score p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The score of each layout shift that did not follow user input.

panels.title: Layout shifts per minute
panels.description: Layout shifts without user input, each minute.

panels.title: INP p75 (time range)
panels.description: Interaction to Next Paint, 75th percentile of the page views in the time range, by navigation type. Good: 200 ms or less. Poor: more than 500 ms.

panels.title: CLS p75 (time range)
panels.description: Cumulative Layout Shift, 75th percentile of the page views in the time range, by navigation type. Good: 0.1 or less. Poor: more than 0.25.

panels.title: LCP p75 (time range)
panels.description: Largest Contentful Paint, 75th percentile of the page views in the time range, by navigation type. Good: 2500 ms or less. Poor: more than 4000 ms.

panels.title: FCP p75 (time range)
panels.description: First Contentful Paint, 75th percentile of the page views in the time range, by navigation type. Good: 1800 ms or less. Poor: more than 3000 ms.

panels.title: TTFB p75 (time range)
panels.description: Time to First Byte, 75th percentile of the page views in the time range, by navigation type. Good: 800 ms or less. Poor: more than 1800 ms.

panels.title: Page views (time range)
panels.description: Page views that reported LCP in the time range: the sample size of the vitals. The count is approximate, because increase() extrapolates.

panels.title: INP p75, by navigation type
panels.description: Interaction to Next Paint p75 of the page views that reported in each interval. The histogram gets one value for each page view, usually when the page is hidden for the first time. Good: 200 ms or less. Poor: more than 500 ms. The dashed lines show the thresholds.

panels.title: CLS p75, by navigation type
panels.description: Cumulative Layout Shift p75 of the page views that reported in each interval. The histogram gets one value for each page view, usually when the page is hidden for the first time. Good: 0.1 or less. Poor: more than 0.25. The dashed lines show the thresholds.

panels.title: LCP p75, by navigation type
panels.description: Largest Contentful Paint p75 of the page views that reported in each interval. The histogram gets one value for each page view, usually when the page is hidden for the first time. Good: 2500 ms or less. Poor: more than 4000 ms. The dashed lines show the thresholds.

panels.title: FCP p75, by navigation type
panels.description: First Contentful Paint p75 of the page views that reported in each interval. The histogram gets one value for each page view, usually when the page is hidden for the first time. Good: 1800 ms or less. Poor: more than 3000 ms. The dashed lines show the thresholds.

panels.title: TTFB p75, by navigation type
panels.description: Time to First Byte p75 of the page views that reported in each interval. The histogram gets one value for each page view, usually when the page is hidden for the first time. Good: 800 ms or less. Poor: more than 1800 ms. The dashed lines show the thresholds.

panels.title: Web Vitals p75 from events, by navigation type
panels.description: From the browser.web_vital events (LogQL unwrap of browser_web_vital_value). A page view sends a new event at each change of a vital, so this p75 includes the earlier values too.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.75, {service_name=~"$service_name", event_name="browser.web_vital"} | service_instance_id=~"$instance" | browser_web_vital_navigation_type=~"$navigation_type" | keep browser_web_vital_name, browser_web_vital_navigation_type, browser_web_vital_value | unwrap browser_web_vital_value [$__range]) by (browser_web_vital_name, browser_web_vital_navigation_type)

sum by (browser_web_vital_name, browser_web_vital_navigation_type) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", event_name="browser.web_vital"} | service_instance_id=~"$instance" | browser_web_vital_navigation_type=~"$navigation_type" | keep browser_web_vital_name, browser_web_vital_navigation_type [$__range]))

panels.title: Web Vitals p75 from events
panels.description: The p75 of browser_web_vital_value for each vital, from the events in a 5-minute window. CLS uses the right axis.

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.75, {service_name=~"$service_name", event_name="browser.web_vital"} | service_instance_id=~"$instance" | browser_web_vital_navigation_type=~"$navigation_type" | keep browser_web_vital_name, browser_web_vital_value | unwrap browser_web_vital_value [5m]) by (browser_web_vital_name)

panels.title: Frames per second, delivered and dropped
panels.description: Animation frames of all visible page loads, each second. Dropped frames are estimated from long gaps between frames.

panels.title: Dropped frame ratio
panels.description: Dropped frames divided by all frames.

panels.title: Frame delta p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The time between two animation frame callbacks. 16.7 ms is 60 frames per second.

panels.title: Idle time remaining p10 / p50 / p90
panels.description: The idle time that was available when an idle callback ran. Low values show a busy main thread.

panels.title: Idle gap p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The time between two idle callbacks.

panels.title: Idle callbacks per minute, by timed_out
panels.description: Idle callbacks, each minute. A callback that timed out ran because no idle period came in time.

panels.title: Idle callbacks that timed out
panels.description: Idle callbacks that timed out, divided by all idle callbacks.

panels.title: Used JS heap p50 / p95, by source
panels.description: The used heap memory of each sample. Modern: performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory(). Legacy: performance.memory.

panels.title: Heap usage ratio p50 / p95
panels.description: The used heap divided by the heap limit. Only the legacy source supplies the limit.

panels.title: Mean pressure state, by source
panels.description: The mean compute pressure state of the records: 0 nominal, 1 fair, 2 serious, 3 critical.

panels.title: Records at serious or critical pressure, by source
panels.description: Records with the state serious (2) or critical (3), divided by all records.

panels.title: GC, page lifecycle and timer throttling
GC events per minute
panels.description: Garbage collections that the GC signal detector saw, each minute, for all page loads.

panels.title: Lifecycle transitions per minute
panels.description: Page lifecycle transitions, each minute, by the states and the trigger event.

panels.title: Throttled timer calibrations
panels.description: Timer calibration rounds that found throttled timers, divided by all rounds. Browsers throttle the timers of hidden pages and of pages in power-saving modes.

panels.title: Browser reports per minute, by type
panels.description: Reports from the Reporting API: interventions and deprecations.

panels.title: Recent browser reports (events)
panels.description: The latest lag.browser_report events.

panels.title: Liveness block duration p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: The duration of each main-thread block that a worker saw through shared memory. Only cross-origin isolated pages have this monitor.

panels.title: Liveness blocks per minute
panels.description: Main-thread blocks that the shared-memory watcher saw, each minute.

panels.title: Events per minute, by event name
panels.description: Lag events in Loki in the minute before each point. event_name is an index label.

panels.title: Page loads
panels.description: The page loads (SDK instances) with lag events in the time range, with the number of events. Set Session to see the page loads of one session. A click on a page load sets the Page load variable: then each panel and each annotation shows only that page load.

targets.expr: topk(50, sum by (service_instance_id, session_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", event_name=~".+"} | service_instance_id=~"$instance" | session_id=~"${session_id:regex}.*" [$__range])))

panels.title: Recent page views and lifecycle transitions
panels.description: The latest lag.page_view.start and lag.lifecycle.transition events. The annotations Page views and Lifecycle show the same events on the charts. Trace: the trace of the page view (lag.page_view.trace_id). A click on it opens the trace in Tempo. The trace shows the view, and its hangs, stalls, long animation frames and hidden periods, with their real start and end. A view whose span was not sampled has no trace.

value.title: Open the trace of the page view in Tempo

panels.title: Recent hangs and stalls
panels.description: The latest lag.main_thread.hang and lag.stall events. The worker sends the hang start itself (scope @lag/worker), because the main thread cannot. An abandoned hang comes from the next page of the origin (Source: journal), another open page (peer), or the page itself at its close (self).

panels.title: Recent clock jumps
panels.description: The latest lag.clock.jump events, with the size of the jump.

panels.title: Page view traces
panels.description: The traces of the page views in the time range, from Tempo: one trace for each view. The root span lag.page_view ends when the page is hidden for the first time in the view. The hangs, stalls, long animation frames and hidden periods of the view are spans in it. An abandoned hang is in the trace of the page that hung. A click on a trace ID opens the trace. Select one page load to see only its views.

panels.title: Long range (recording rules, all page loads)
p95 by service (recorded)
panels.description: From the recording rules service_name:<metric>:p95_rate5m (5-minute windows, evaluated each minute). Use these panels for long time ranges. The rules sum all page loads, thus the Page load variable does not apply here.

panels.title: p99 by service (recorded)
panels.description: From the recording rules service_name:<metric>:p99_rate5m.

panels.title: Fleet p95 from recorded rates
panels.description: The p95 of all selected services, from the recorded native-histogram rates service_name:<metric>:rate5m. A sum of recorded rates is correct; a sum of recorded quantiles is not.

panels.title: Web Vitals p75 from recorded rates
panels.description: The p75 of each vital, from the recorded rates service_name_navigation_type:<metric>:rate5m. CLS uses the right axis.
